stage_a.note: Founder communicates strong, sustained positive engagement and confidence throughout the prepared presentation.
Founder speaks with energy and clear excitement about solving the loose change problem.
The presentation is polite and approachable, but predominantly business-focused.

venture.description: A digital platform that allows retail customers to save their loose change into a digital wallet using their phone number.
venture.note: The platform serves both consumers and merchants.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Founder introduces the company and demonstrates how the digital wallet works at the point of sale.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin asks if he pays with his account the next time he gets a coffee.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jeff explains the four cash-out options, including bank transfer, Amazon gift cards, charity, or redeeming in-store.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin asks how Jeff plans to avoid being crushed by giant payment operators long-term.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jeff responds that no one has done this because the industry incorrectly assumes cash is going away.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin challenges Jeff on whether that is his entire answer.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jeff insists cash is not going away.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark challenges the idea that anyone thinks cash is going away.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark states that even bitcoin enthusiasts don't believe cash will disappear.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin asserts that Jeff is going to get crushed.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jeff argues that their technology is difficult to build and requires complex banking relationships and regulatory structures.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Barbara asks what incentive the retailer has to install the screen.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jeff states that cash handling is very expensive for retailers, citing armored truck deliveries for coins.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Barbara agrees, mentioning that her local pizzeria receives armored truck deliveries for coins.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jeff adds that beyond cost savings, the system acts as an effective loyalty program for the retailer.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin claims the barista is looking at Jeff with fear because she knows he is a dead man walking.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jeff explains that the loyalty program builds connective tissue between the merchant and previously anonymous cash customers.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin agrees that it is a great idea.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert adds that he hates carrying change.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Barbara jokes that Robert hates carrying change because he's rich.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert asks Jeff to explain the revenue model.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jeff states they charge merchants twenty dollars a month.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark asks to clarify the twenty dollars a month figure.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jeff confirms twenty dollars a month and adds they earn three percent on each transaction.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jeff shares his background story of leaving a corporate law path to start his venture after watching Shark Tank.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert asks to confirm if Jeff had a full-time offer at Apple.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jeff confirms he turned down an offer at Apple and a clear path to corporate law to pursue this.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori asks how much money Jeff has invested.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jeff answers they have raised four hundred sixty thousand dollars from family, friends, and his own money.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark points out that getting people to use the application is the main issue and it will not be cheap.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jeff agrees with Mark's point.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark argues it is difficult to extract twenty dollars a month given all the applications a barista could run.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jeff acknowledges the point but insists change remains a large unsolved problem.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark says he solves it by using a credit card.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jeff argues that numbers tell a different story, citing that many transactions are still cash and loyalty programs miss these customers.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Barbara compliments Jeff for standing his ground and treating Mark and Kevin as equals.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert asks Jeff to tell them what is currently working in the business.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jeff shares that they have completed twenty-five hundred transactions in four months and customers love it.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert asserts that the core problem solved is for people who dislike change, making loyalty just an added benefit.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jeff agrees with Robert.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark asks to confirm the mechanism of storing the phone number and accumulating data in the cloud.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jeff confirms Mark's understanding of the technology.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark praises the cloud tracking idea but calls focusing solely on CoinOut horrific.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jeff acknowledges Mark's disagreement regarding the dual challenge of consumer and barista awareness.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark states he has a problem with focusing on one feature instead of a broader solution and exits.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jeff accepts Mark's decision.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori exits because she is unsure how the business will ensure a return on her investment.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jeff pushes back, arguing that reaching a hundred thousand locations would yield a thirty million dollar run rate.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Barbara asks how long it will take to get one thousand retailers.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jeff expects to reach seven hundred locations by year end and three thousand next year.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Barbara states she believes he will make it happen.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Barbara makes an offer contingent on Jeff getting those locations by the end of the year.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jeff rejects the offer, calling the contingency untenable.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Barbara asks why he won't accept if he previously said he could hit the numbers.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jeff reiterates he will not do a contingency based on locations.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Barbara presses him on his earlier claim of being able to get the locations.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jeff states he believes he can, but it is not in his interest to make the deal dependent on it.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Barbara says his response makes her lose confidence.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jeff asserts his confidence and says a short-term contingency implies a lack of belief in the vision.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin interjects that Jeff doesn't believe in himself.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jeff tells Kevin he wouldn't make that deal himself, though he'd consider it if it were his only offer.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Barbara insists he lacks the confidence he suggested earlier.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jeff maintains that he does have the confidence.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Barbara exits, citing her own experience of guaranteeing a return when she borrowed money.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jeff accepts Barbara's decision.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin prepares to make an offer, asking how much pain Jeff is willing to take.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin makes an offer without a contingency but for higher equity.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jeff thanks Kevin and says he wants to hear other offers.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin argues the extra equity is the cost of Jeff's unwillingness to accept a contingency.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jeff says he hasn't felt love from Kevin and isn't sure he should consider the offer.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin replies that it's about money, not love.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert makes an offer, contingent on a successful pilot with a large-scale retailer.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jeff accepts the contingency but counters the equity ask.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert reminds Jeff of Kevin's competing offer.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jeff argues that they have proven the technology and the market size to justify his counter.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert tells Jeff he won't move and urges a decision.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jeff asks if Robert is completely unwilling to move on the equity.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert confirms he is not moving, emphasizing the need to see the concept proven in reality.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jeff counters again, asking for a slight reduction in the equity.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert points out Jeff's hesitation over a small percentage difference.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jeff explains his counter was the highest he originally wanted to go.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert states firmly that his offer remains at fifteen percent.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jeff accepts Robert's offer, joking that Kevin can't use the product.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert confirms the deal is done.

decisions.note: Exits because the founder is focused on only one feature rather than a bigger solution.
Exits because she is unsure how she will get her investment back.

decisions.terms: $250,000 for 15% equity, contingent on obtaining 700 locations by year end.
decisions.note: Believes the locations are the missing key to the program.
Rejects the contingency based on locations.
Exits because the founder lacks the confidence to guarantee the locations.
Offers a deal without a contingency but for higher equity.

decisions.terms: $250,000 for 15% equity, contingent upon a successful pilot with a large retailer.
decisions.note: Wants to see the concept proven out with a large retailer.
Accepts the contingency but counters the equity.
Counters with the maximum equity he originally wanted to give up.

record.notes: The female helper acting as a barista is not recorded as an actor because she does not speak. F1's turn 25 is recorded as NONE as it is a transition into a personal story without a question.
